Some games don't need goals. Minecraft's goal of The End is only loosely in people's consciousness. Most people just play to zone out, explore, build things, etc. Survival mode has always seemed somewhat borked to me, and it's easy to get to a place where nothing can ever realistically hurt you. But the expressive quality of that game is amazing.

And even for me now, I'm playing Diablo 3, and I'm pretty much out of goals. I've beaten the game, I'm on Torment X with my Demon Hunter. But I keep playing because the fundamental gameplay loop is fun and engaging. Plus I'm hoping to complete a different set and try a totally different build for my DH, which will bridge the way to an entirely different gameplay loop.

Hell, lately I've been crazy addicted to a game called Twenty. And the only "goal" in that is to go for a highscore. So far my highest is 11. But the visceral act of playing is really fun.

The problem with No Man's Sky, from the people shitting on it, is that the gameplay loop is simply boring. You shoot things with your laser, and feed what you get into various shrinking bars to make them not shrink. Sometimes you can upgrade the bars to shrink slower. But the gameplay lacks any sort of visceral quality to it the way an action game might, or the sort of self expression a game like Minecraft offers. Nor does it really have the sense of exploration it was aiming for because you rapidly see through the mixed and matched parts involved in the procedural generation. Nor do you find anything actually different, from a gameplay perspective, thanks to your exploration. It's just a reskin of what you did on the last planet.

Sure, there are games where exploration is a big part of the play. But exploration in an of itself is not crux of player accomplishment. Using Minecraft as an example, exploring will get you unique block materials and crafting components, as well as mob types. If it was just wandering around without crafting and building, then no one would play. That's why most 'walking simulator' games get panned - there's no accomplishment built into the game loop. Diablo's fun because you like to make baddies explode into gold and loot, and that never gets old. But for No Man's Sky, landing on Planet Umpteenth C-43 to see some terrain and a couple creatures again and again doesn't sound that interesting.
